title: Base change for a composite square
statement:
Consider a tower of Cartesian diagrams of schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W & \xleftarrow{j} & Z\\
i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow k\\
X & \xleftarrow{h} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{g} & T
\end{array}
$$

and let $K\in D(T_{\Et})$. If

$$
f^{-1}Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*e^{-1}K
\quad\text{and}\quad
i^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rj_*k^{-1}e^{-1}K
$$

are isomorphisms, then
$(f\circ i)^{-1}Rg_*K\to Rj_*(e\circ k)^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism
(``the outer rectangle'') and the analogous statement holds
degreewise for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ and the maps
$R^q$.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma [Tag `0EZS`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZS).*)
The derived maps here are the unbounded exchange morphisms of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$; the degreewise maps are those of [sbc-def-base-change-map], for each integer $q\ge0$, without requiring isomorphisms in other degrees.

proof.text:
The outer rectangle is Cartesian by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], applied to the displayed diagram with left and right columns interchanged. Write $c_{f,i}:i^{-1}f^{-1}\cong(fi)^{-1}$ and $c_{e,k}:k^{-1}e^{-1}\cong(ek)^{-1}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. These sheaf isomorphisms act termwise on arbitrary complexes. In the equations below, $c_{u,v}$ on the unbounded derived category means the unique descent of this termwise comparison under clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with the localization comparison isomorphisms of [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]. All equations are read with these comparisons inserted. For the lower and upper squares the sheaf-level formula (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting], with $(f,f',g,g')=(g,h,f,e)$ and $(h,h',f'')=(i,k,j)$, gives
$$\theta_{\mathrm{out}}\circ(j^{-1}c_{f,i})=(c_{e,k}g^{-1})\circ(k^{-1}\theta_1)\circ(\theta_2f^{-1}).$$
The same equality holds termwise on complexes. Exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] induces the unbounded functors and comparisons by [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]; descending the equality along localization preserves composition and equality by clauses (2),(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus this displayed equation holds on the full unbounded derived categories, not just their bounded below subcategories.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_K:f^{-1}Rg_*K\to Rh_*e^{-1}K$ and $\beta_L:i^{-1}Rh_*L\to Rj_*k^{-1}L$ be the two exchange maps of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], taking $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with $(L_1,R_1)=(g^{-1},Rg_*)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(h^{-1},Rh_*)$, $(L_3,R_3)=(j^{-1},Rj_*)$, $(G,H)=(f^{-1},e^{-1})$, $(G_2,H_2)=(i^{-1},k^{-1})$, and square transformations $\theta_1,\theta_2$. The mate of $P=(k^{-1}\theta_1)\circ(\theta_2f^{-1})$ is $(\beta e^{-1})\circ(i^{-1}\alpha)$. Step 1 says $\theta_{\mathrm{out}}=(c_{e,k}g^{-1})\circ P\circ(j^{-1}c_{f,i}^{-1})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker], with $\sigma=c_{f,i}^{-1}$ and $\tau=c_{e,k}$, its mate is therefore
$$\gamma_K=Rj_*(c_{e,k,K})\circ\beta_{e^{-1}K}\circ i^{-1}(\alpha_K)\circ c_{f,i,Rg_*K}^{-1}.$$
This identifies the actual outer exchange morphism, including both comparison maps.

source.place: Tag 0EZS, label lemma-base-change-compose, proof; Sites Cohomology Tag 0E47, label remark-compose-base-change-horizontal

proof.text: Under the derived hypotheses $\alpha_K$ and $\beta_{e^{-1}K}$ are isomorphisms. Any functor takes an inverse to an inverse, since it preserves composition and identities. Thus $i^{-1}(\alpha_K)$ and $Rj_*(c_{e,k,K})$ are isomorphisms; $c_{f,i,Rg_*K}^{-1}$ is already a comparison isomorphism. The inverse of the product in step 2 is the product of these four inverses in reverse order. Hence $\gamma_K$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0EZS, label lemma-base-change-compose, proof; Sites Cohomology Tag 0E47, label remark-compose-base-change-horizontal

proof.text: For the independent degreewise assertion, take $K=\mathcal F[0]$ and apply $H^q$ to the equality in step 2. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], for any representative complex $C$ one has $i^{-1}\Ker d^q=\Ker(i^{-1}d^q)$ and $i^{-1}\operatorname{Im}d^{q-1}=\operatorname{Im}(i^{-1}d^{q-1})$, and inverse image preserves their quotient. Consequently $H^q(i^{-1}C)=i^{-1}H^q(C)$, naturally also for maps (apply this to the maps of representatives of a derived roof). Using the degreewise definition [sbc-def-base-change-map] and $R^qu_*\mathcal F=H^q(Ru_*\mathcal F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the resulting middle factors are precisely $i^{-1}(\alpha^q_{\mathcal F})$ and $\beta^q_{e^{-1}\mathcal F}$. The outside factors are cohomology of comparison isomorphisms, hence are isomorphisms. If the two degree-$q$ maps in the hypothesis are isomorphisms, the inverse-product argument of step 3 proves the degree-$q$ outer map is an isomorphism. No assertion about any other cohomology degree was used.
